test_title: PYST 90: SSC GD Constable - English (Held On - 06 Mar, 2024 Shift 4)
subject: english
question: What does the idiom "the ball is in your court" mean?

options.text: A very small part of something big or whole
The situation or decision is now up to you
A sceptic who needs physical or personal evidence in order to believe something.
Anything that is common and easy to get.

solution: The correct answer is: **Option 2** i.e. The situation or decision is now up to you. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** __ • The idiom **"the ball is in your court"** means the situation or decision is now up to you. (अब फैसला या स्थिति आपके हाथ में है) • **Example:** I have done all I can; now the ball is in your court to decide what to do next. Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 2** i.e. The situation or decision is now up to you. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences: • **Option 1:** A very small part of something big or whole (कुछ बड़ा या संपूर्ण का बहुत छोटा हिस्सा) • **Example:** The single page you found is just a drop in the ocean compared to the entire report. • **Option 3:** A sceptic who needs physical or personal evidence in order to believe something. (एक संदेहवादी जिसे किसी चीज़ पर विश्वास करने के लिए भौतिक या व्यक्तिगत प्रमाण की आवश्यकता होती है) • **Example:** As a doubting Thomas, he needs to see concrete evidence before he believes in the project. • **Option 4:** Anything that is common and easy to get. (कोई भी चीज़ जो सामान्य और आसानी से प्राप्त होने वाली हो) • **Example:** These days, smartphones are a dime a dozen; everyone has one. 35:Tc0b, The correct answer is **Option 1**.
